items.prompt: PageService.GetTreeAsync groups pages with ToLookup(p => p.ParentId) rather than a Dictionary. Why?
items.answer: Roots have a null ParentId, which a Dictionary key cannot hold
distractors: ToLookup keeps sibling Position order, which a Dictionary loses
A Dictionary would load every page twice from the database
ToLookup runs in SQL while a Dictionary is built in memory
items.explanation: A lookup accepts the null key for roots and returns an empty sequence for parents without children.

items.prompt: A user drags page A under one of A's own grandchildren. What does the move do?
items.answer: It is refused: a page cannot move under itself or any descendant
distractors: It succeeds and the grandchild becomes A's new parent
It moves A to the root and clamps its Position to 0
It succeeds, and the cycle is broken lazily on the next tree load
items.explanation: Moves are clamped into range and are cycle-safe via DescendantIdsAsync; Reindex keeps sibling positions contiguous 0..n-1.

items.prompt: The Page parent FK uses DeleteBehavior.Restrict. How is a subtree removed then?
items.answer: Explicitly in the service, so the database never cascades silently
distractors: By the database cascade, which Restrict enables for self-references
By a nightly cleanup job that deletes orphaned pages
It cannot be removed until each child is deleted by hand in the UI
items.explanation: Restrict prevents a silent cascade; the service performs subtree removal deliberately (blocks follow the same rule).

items.prompt: Under which block type may child blocks nest?
distractors: Under any Heading or Callout
Under any block, up to three levels
Only under a Table, as rows
items.explanation: ParentBlockId is validated in BlockService.ValidateParentAsync; blocks come back as a flat pre-order DFS list the client re-nests.

items.prompt: A member of workspace X requests a page id from workspace Y. Another member requests a Private page in their own workspace that they do not own. What do they get?
items.answer: Not found for the foreign page; forbidden for the private one
distractors: Forbidden for both, since neither caller may read the page
Not found for both, so no page's existence is ever revealed
A login redirect for the foreign page; not found for the private one
items.explanation: Cross-workspace existence is hidden with 404; a visible-but-forbidden resource is 403 (ADR 0002).

items.prompt: An Editor opens a Workspace-visible page whose share permission is View. What can they do?
items.answer: Read it (200) but not write it (403)
distractors: Read and write it, because Editors always write
Neither: View shares are for Viewers only
Write it, but only through the version restore
items.explanation: Writes need share = Edit for Editors; Owners can always write; Viewers never write.

items.prompt: Which actions need only read access on a page?
distractors: Duplicating and templating
Sharing and versioning
Creating child pages and editing blocks
items.explanation: Viewers can comment and star; creating pages, editing blocks, sharing, versioning, duplicating and templating are writes.

items.prompt: What happens first when a page is restored to version 3?
items.answer: The current state is snapshotted as 'Before restore to v3'
distractors: Every version newer than v3 is deleted from history
The blocks are replaced first, and then a diff of the change is logged
A copy of the page is created holding v3's blocks
items.explanation: Restore is non-destructive; snapshot block ids are reused, so toggle parent references survive (ADR 0005).

items.prompt: ActivityService.Add appends an Activity row without calling SaveChanges. What does that guarantee?
items.answer: The activity commits in the same transaction as the mutation
distractors: The activity is written later, by a background flush after the response
The activity is lost if the request is cancelled
The activity becomes visible to readers before the mutation commits
items.explanation: The calling service's SaveChangesAsync persists both together.

items.prompt: The page author is also mentioned in a new comment and has commented before. How many notifications do they get?
items.answer: One, because recipients are deduplicated with a HashSet
distractors: Three, one notification for each reason they qualify
Two: one for the mention and one for authorship
None, because page authors are excluded from fan-out
items.explanation: Recipients = mentioned ∪ author ∪ prior commenters, minus the actor; prior commenters are read before the new comment saves.

items.prompt: An outgoing link points at a page that has since been made private to the caller. How is it shown?
items.answer: As broken, with the stored token title instead of the live title
distractors: As a normal link that returns 403 when the caller clicks it
Hidden entirely, as if the block text contained no link
As a normal link showing the target page's current title
items.explanation: Treating unseeable targets as broken stops the current title leaking; it mirrors backlink visibility filtering (ADR 0006).

items.prompt: Page and Block carry a Guid Version. What happens to a write that omits ExpectedVersion?
items.answer: The concurrency check is skipped, for backward compatibility
distractors: It is rejected with 409 Conflict, since the version is required
It is rejected with 428 Precondition Required
It is queued until the client fetches a fresh version
items.explanation: A mismatched ExpectedVersion gives 409; the Guid rotates on every successful write because SQLite has no native rowversion (ADR 0009).

items.prompt: Why must UseRateLimiter run after UseAuthentication in Folio's pipeline?
items.answer: The limiter partitions by user id, which comes from authentication
distractors: Authentication itself is rate-limited, so its requests must count first
The limiter needs CORS headers set by authentication
Rate limiting only applies to anonymous public endpoints
items.explanation: It is a partitioned fixed-window limiter on writes only; GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, auth, public and health are exempt; exceeding returns 429.

items.prompt: Why does Folio store timestamps as UTC DateTime rather than DateTimeOffset?
items.answer: SQLite cannot order or compare DateTimeOffset values
distractors: DateTimeOffset doubles the storage size of each row
The React client cannot parse offset strings
EF Core migrations reject DateTimeOffset columns
items.explanation: ADR 0008 records the choice; enums are stored as strings for readability and stability against reordering.

items.front: How does Folio make sure the EF model and migrations never drift apart?
items.back: The app applies migrations at startup (Database.Migrate(), not EnsureCreated) and a MigrationGuardTests test fails the build if the model drifts from the migrations (ADR 0003).

items.front: How do public page links work, and how is one revoked?
items.back: A Public page gets a random PublicSlug readable anonymously at GET /api/public/pages/{slug}. Changing visibility away from Public clears the slug, revoking the link immediately; the slug has a filtered unique index (unique only where non-null).

Page.IsFavorite is one page-level boolean, not per member: starring a page stars it for the whole workspace. Intentional simplification; notification targeting avoids depending on per-user favorites (ADR 0007).

items.front: How is soft delete implemented, and how do trash/restore see deleted pages?
items.back: Page.IsDeleted drives a global query filter HasQueryFilter(p => !p.IsDeleted); trash and restore paths opt out with IgnoreQueryFilters().
